_what_this_is: The authoritative source for every fixed value, definition and term in this MVP. It mirrors the package canon (12_Canon.json in the VIP SmartContract package) for everything the two share. Where this file and any document or code comment disagree, this file is correct.
_stability: Code, wording and the console may improve in any later revision; the thresholds, splits, model figures and event vocabulary below do not change with them. The verification line is the one exception and says so where it stands: it counts checks, so it moves when a check is added. Restated in canon 1.14: the event vocabulary grew in v0.2.14 by the two types of the pre-stake check, stake.refused and stake.exceeded, which the package canon fixes as well; every earlier type keeps its meaning.
canon_change_log: 1.0 — first canon for the VIP MVP, which is the first runnable build this product line has had. No value is invented: every threshold, split and model figure is lifted from the package canon at v3.5, and the two figures the seed needs beyond it are labelled where they appear.

mechanism.definition: A policy engine that turns a responsible-gambling limit into a revenue event: the guest pre-commits a budget, the engine watches the session, and at the threshold it stops gaming and converts the preserved budget into non-gaming spend and rollover credit.
mechanism.flow: pre-commit → session ticks → policy stop at threshold → rollover + redirect issuance → hash-anchored audit
mechanism.position: Middleware. Funds never go on chain, rules stay off chain, only proofs are hash-anchored.
mechanism.what_it_is_not: Not a wallet or payments rail, not a detection or risk-scoring model, not a CRM journey engine. It consumes risk signals and produces a policy decision and a revenue event.

03a_hard_stop.name: Hard-Stop
03a_hard_stop.rule: at the threshold the engine locks the session, with no override: every further tick is refused, and the lock is answered with 423 rather than an error. The lock falls on the line itself where the platform checks each stake before accepting it (POST /v3/session/authorize) and no wager consumes more than its check; consumption reported only after the fact is counted in full, the lock falls on the tick that crosses the line, and the stop records how far past the line consumption went (overshoot_eur). A pre-commitment binds for the commitment period: while a session is live and younger than VIP_COMMITMENT_HOURS, a new pre-commit for the same guest is refused with SESSION_LIVE. From v0.2.16 a stopped session holds the guest for the same period, counted from when it was armed, and a new pre-commit is refused with COMMITMENT_ACTIVE; the engine keeps no calendar, so a gaming day that ends at a fixed hour remains the operator's rule

03b_advisory.name: Advisory
03b_advisory.rule: the engine nudges the guest with a live incentive preview, then escalates to the host; there is no lock, and a stop happens only if the guest chooses it

modes._rule: Both modes run the SAME engine, and in this build they run the same function: an enforced stop and a voluntary stop settle through one code path, so the incentive mechanics cannot drift apart between them. Mode is carried on the pre-commit call; a call that leaves it out runs the deployment's configured mode, VIP_MODE, and the response names the mode it armed.

thresholds._rollover_switch: VIP_FUTURE_PLAY=off sets the rollover to 0, whatever VIP_ROLLOVER says, and leaves that share with the guest; any value other than on or off refuses to start. Default on, at one fifth, so no figure here changes.

_prose.hard_stop_fraction: Half of the pre-committed budget. Remains a per-jurisdiction configurable.
_prose.advisory_nudge_fraction: Four tenths of the pre-committed budget: the guest is shown exactly what stopping now would earn.
_prose.advisory_escalate_fraction: Eighty-five hundredths of the pre-committed budget: the engine escalates to the host with the numbers already computed.
_prose.rollover_fraction: One fifth of preserved budget, issued as rollover credit toward a future session. It is a liability, not revenue, until the guest returns and uses it.
_prose.redirect_split: Seven tenths of preserved budget in total, issued as resort credit, divided spa 0.30, F&B 0.25, retail 0.15 of preserved budget. This is the non-gaming capture figure every document quotes.
_prose.residual_to_guest_fraction: One tenth of preserved budget is neither redirected nor rolled over. It is the guest's own residual and is returned. Named so the model closes: redirect + rollover + residual is the whole preserved budget.
_prose._configurability_rule: Every threshold above — including each of the three redirect shares — is a per-jurisdiction configurable, not a hard constant, and each is read from its own environment variable named in config_authority. This build validates each one at startup and REFUSES TO START on a value that is not a finite number in range, because a comparison against a non-finite threshold is false in JavaScript and would silently turn the limit into a gate that admits everything. It also refuses to start when rollover plus redirect would exceed the preserved budget.
_prose._money_rule: Every decision that involves money is taken on integer cents, and every configured fraction is read as an integer number of millionths, rounded to the nearest. Each line — stop, nudge, escalation — is the first whole cent at or above its fraction of the budget and fires on that cent; armed_at_eur publishes the stop line, so the number the guest is told is the number at which the engine acts. The settlement divides the preserved budget by the largest-remainder method on integer cents, a tie going to the earlier position: first across redirect, rollover and residual, then across spa, F&B and retail inside the redirect. A budget is accepted from €0.01 to €10,000,000 and a single tick up to €10,000,000, the range in which every product the engine forms is an exact integer. A budget that carries a fraction of a cent is taken to the nearest cent on arrival; consumption is kept as the exact total of the ticks reported, so ticks below a cent still add up, and every decision reads that total in whole cents — the stop, the display and the settlement alike — so while consumption is within the budget, consumed plus preserved is the budget to the cent.

eligibility_gate._what_it_is: A gate in front of the incentive, not in front of the stop. It decides whether a settlement may ISSUE, never whether a guest is at risk. This engine performs no risk assessment and holds no harm model.
eligibility_gate._why_it_is_an_input: The operator's responsible-gaming determination arrives as an input, per session, or as a programme-level suppression. A policy layer that classified harm would be a responsible-gaming system and would fall inside the certification perimeter of every jurisdiction that has one. This one stays a policy layer.
eligibility_gate.composition_rule: The stricter of the configured default and the per-session input always wins, and a programme-level suppression overrides both. A jurisdiction that forbids the incentive outright sets the default to suppressed and no session can re-enable it.
eligibility_gate._reference_note: Every metric and model figure in this canon was computed at the reference value, which is the gate open. A stricter setting lowers realised retention and realised redirect in that deployment; it does not make any figure here wrong, because the figures state what the mechanism produces at the stated configuration. This is the same rule the redirect split already follows.
eligibility_gate.suppressed_settlement: The stop still fires and the budget is still preserved. Nothing is issued: redirect 0, rollover 0, and the whole preserved amount returns to the guest as residual. Suppression removes the incentive, never the protection.

reward_cap_eur._what_it_is: An absolute euro ceiling on the operator-funded part of a settlement — redirect plus rollover.
reward_cap_eur._why_it_exists: Without a ceiling the incentive grows with the pre-committed budget, so a larger declared budget earns a larger reward. That is an incentive to declare a larger budget, and it is the one attack on this design the mechanism does not answer by itself.
reward_cap_eur._reference_note: Off means uncapped, which is the configuration every figure in this canon was computed under. From v0.2.16 the ceiling is on by default at €5,000 per stop; VIP_REWARD_CAP_EUR=off switches it off. The reference stop preserves €5,100 and earns €4,590, under the default, so every figure in this canon holds under the default as well.
reward_cap_eur.binding_behaviour: When the cap binds, the excess is not retained by the operator. It goes to the guest as residual, so a capped settlement returns more of the guest's own money, never less, and the model still closes: redirect + rollover + residual = preserved.

eligibility_lifetime_days._what_it_is: How long the operator's responsible-gaming determination stays good for, in days.
eligibility_lifetime_days._why_it_exists: A determination taken once and never revisited is the weakest form of a control. Supervisory expectations in several regimes include periodic review of a high-value customer's account, and a policy layer that honours a two-year-old assessment as though it were today's is honouring a memory of a control rather than the control.
eligibility_lifetime_days._reference_note: Off means the determination never expires, which is the configuration every figure in this canon was computed under. From v0.2.16 the lifetime is on by default at 90 days; VIP_ELIGIBILITY_TTL_DAYS=off switches it off. The seed records a fresh determination on every session, so the seeded quarter is the canon quarter under the default as well. A pre-commit that carries no determination date issues nothing under the default.
eligibility_lifetime_days.fail_direction: CLOSED. When the lifetime elapses the incentive is withheld until the operator supplies a fresh determination; the stop and the preserved budget are unaffected and the whole preserved amount returns to the guest. An ABSENT determination date is treated as expired rather than as fresh, because an unknown age is not a young age, and a date that does not parse is refused at pre-commit with INVALID_ELIGIBILITY_AT. Failing open would mean issuing value on stale grounds, which is the thing the lifetime exists to prevent.
eligibility_lifetime_days.recorded_separately: An expiry writes eligibility.expired, distinct from incentive.suppressed. A decision to withhold and a failure to refresh are different facts and a reader of the chain must be able to tell them apart.

thresholds._settlement_closure: The settlement is allocated in integer CENTS by the largest-remainder method, not by rounding each leg independently. Two invariants hold for every amount, and the suite asserts them exhaustively from €0.01 to €2,000.00 rather than on a sample: spa + fnb + retail === redirect, and redirect + rollover + residual === preserved. No leg is ever negative. Before v3.10 the legs were rounded independently and failed to close on 52,205 of the 200,000 amounts from €0.01 to €2,000.00 — roughly one in four — by one cent in either direction; every figure printed in this canon is unchanged by the correction, because at these figures the shares divide exactly. Closing is necessary and not sufficient: v3.16 closed on every one of those amounts and still put a cent into a different venue than the largest-remainder rule on 6,553 of them, because a floating-point remainder decided ties that position should decide. From v3.17 money is decided on integers (_prose._money_rule), and the suite recomputes the rule itself, independently, on every amount in the same range.

commitment_period_hours._what_it_is: How long a pre-commitment binds, counted from the moment it was armed. While a session is live and younger than this, a new pre-commit for the same guest is refused with SESSION_LIVE; from v0.2.16, while the guest's latest session has stopped inside the same period, it is refused with COMMITMENT_ACTIVE. Both answers name the session and the time from which a new pre-commit will be accepted.
commitment_period_hours._why_it_exists: Until v0.2.13 any pre-commit replaced a live session at once, so one call with a larger budget moved the line in the middle of play. A limit that the next call can raise is not a pre-commitment.
commitment_period_hours._after_the_period: A live session may be superseded as before; it is closed and kept, and its open checks close with it. A stopped guest may commit again. This is how the next budget is armed.
commitment_period_hours._zero: 0 switches both holds off: a pre-commit supersedes a live session at once, and a stopped guest may commit again at once. It is an operator-side setting and is stated as one.
commitment_period_hours._clock: The age is read from the wall clock. A session whose opening lies in the future, after a clock set backwards, stays held, live or stopped: the lock fails closed.
commitment_period_hours._stopped_sessions: Until v0.2.15 a stopped session did not hold the guest, so a guest stopped by the line could arm a second budget at once, and a second limit on top of the first was one call away. From v0.2.16 the stop holds the guest for the rest of the period. The engine keeps no calendar: the period is counted in hours from arming, and a gaming day that ends at a fixed hour remains the property's own rule.

_prose.hard_stop_fired: 423 Locked is the contract's own signal that the Hard-Stop fired: the session is locked and its settlement computed, and POST /v3/redirect/issue then issues the credits and the rollover — or refuses, if the incentive is withheld. It is a state, not an error — the stop is the product working. From v0.2.14 the answer carries overshoot_eur: 0 when the line held, and how far past it consumption went when the crossing amount reached the engine without a check.
_prose.stake_authorized: 200 on POST /v3/session/authorize: the stake fits in what is left to the line and is reserved against it until the tick that reports it, or a release, closes the check. The answer carries authorization_id, session_id, the stake to the cent, enforced (true in Hard-Stop, false in Advisory, where nothing is refused), reserved_eur and headroom_eur. A stake that does not fit is not a 2xx: it is 409 STAKE_EXCEEDS_HEADROOM, the Hard-Stop working before the stake rather than after it.
_prose.stake_released: 200 on POST /v3/session/release: a checked stake that was never played, a cancelled or voided wager, returns its reservation to the headroom, and nothing is consumed.
_prose.terms_published: 200 on GET /v3/terms: the terms a guest agrees to — the stop line, the advisory lines, the split of the preserved budget, the rollover and the residual, the ceiling on the incentive, the eligibility default, the determination lifetime and the commitment period — and terms_version, 'terms-' and the leading 12 hex characters of the SHA-256 of those values serialised with their keys sorted. Slot 04b computes it the same way, so the same terms carry the same version in both services.

surfaces.spec_routes: /v3/* — the architecture contract an integrator implements in their own platform. Paths, status codes, error identifiers and response fields are those of registry slot 04b_Integration_Reference.js on every route, except the fields inside each event on the audit route, which are this build's own record; a client written against the reference runs against this build unchanged as long as it reads amounts from the tick and state responses.
surfaces.product_routes: /vip/* and the HTML console — the product surface of this running system: voluntary stop, credit redemption, rollover application, the quarter roll-up, chain verification and erasure.
surfaces.note: The two are different layers. The /v3 routes are served here so the contract is demonstrable; the /vip routes exist only in this evaluation build and are not part of the specification.

error_identifiers._rule: Errors have an error identifier. A 423 locked response is a successful policy stop with a settlement body. See 04_API_Spec.yaml.
error_identifiers._contract_scope: Observable by a caller of the /v3 surface.
error_identifiers._product_scope: Raised only on /vip/* routes and, for UNAUTHORIZED, on GET /admin — none of them part of the specification.

_prose.NO_LIVE_SESSION: A call arrived for a VIP with no session on record, or for one whose session was superseded, including a vip_id that is not a string, which names none. A check or a release that names a session_id other than the current one is answered the same way.
_prose.INVALID_VIP: Missing or non-string vip_id on the pre-commit or the suppression call.
_prose.INVALID_BUDGET: Budget absent, non-numeric, below one cent or above €10,000,000. Outside that range the engine cannot arm a line it decides exactly.
_prose.INVALID_MODE: Mode is neither hard_stop nor advisory.
_prose.INVALID_DELTA: The consumption delta is absent, null, non-numeric, NEGATIVE, or above €10,000,000. A tick reports consumption, which only goes up; a negative delta was accepted by slot 04b until v3.11 and silently reduced consumption, which lets a caller walk a session back from its stop line. Validated at the boundary so a malformed tick can never move consumption. Corrections, if an integration needs them, belong on their own route with their own link in the chain.
_prose.ALREADY_STOPPED: A tick arrived for a session the policy has already stopped.
_prose.NOT_STOPPED: Redirect requested before the policy fired. Credits are issued from preserved budget, which only exists after a stop.
_prose.ALREADY_ISSUED: Redirect requested twice for the same session. Credits are issued once.
_prose.SESSION_UNKNOWN: No audit rows exist for that session id.
_prose.NO_ROUTE: No route matches the request; the response names the nine contract routes.
_prose.BAD_JSON: The request body does not parse as JSON, or parses to something other than a JSON object — null, an array, a bare string or number. Returned by the transport layer before any handler runs.
_prose.BAD_REQUEST: The request target cannot be read: the request line is not a parseable URL, or the session_id on an audit path is not valid percent-encoding. Answered before the request reaches the engine.
_prose.CREDIT_UNKNOWN: No issued credit carries that identifier. A credit is identified by the positive integer it was issued under, sent as a JSON number; a string, a boolean or a fraction identifies none.
_prose.CREDIT_REDEEMED: That credit has already been redeemed. Redemption happens once.
_prose.NO_ROLLOVER: The guest holds no unapplied rollover credit, or the call names no guest — a missing or non-string vip_id.
_prose.GUEST_UNKNOWN: No guest carries that identifier, or the call names no guest — a missing or non-string vip_id.
_prose.ALREADY_ERASED: Erasure was already performed for that guest.
_prose.UNAUTHORIZED: The admin token is missing or wrong on a route that requires it.
_prose.INVALID_ELIGIBILITY: the eligibility value supplied at pre-commit is not one of permitted | suppressed.
_prose.INVALID_REASON: the suppression reason is not one of exclusion | player_request | rg_determination.
_prose.INCENTIVE_SUPPRESSED: a redirect was requested on a session whose incentive is withheld, or a credit redemption or a rollover application arrived for a guest who has been suppressed, whatever the reason. The stop and the preserved budget are unaffected.
_prose.ALREADY_SUPPRESSED: this guest is already out of the programme. Suppression is not reversible by this engine.
_prose.INVALID_ELIGIBILITY_AT: A supplied determination must have a valid calendar date, time and timezone and cannot be in the future.
_prose.INVALID_STAKE: The stake on a check is absent, not a finite number, below one cent or above €10,000,000. A stake is taken to the nearest cent, as a budget is.
_prose.STAKE_EXCEEDS_HEADROOM: In Hard-Stop, the stake is larger than what is left to the line once every stake checked and not yet reported is counted as lost. It is refused before it is placed, the refusal is written to the chain as stake.refused although the request fails, and the answer names headroom_eur, the largest stake the check would allow now. Advisory mode never answers it.
_prose.AUTHORIZATION_UNKNOWN: A tick or a release names a check that this guest's current session never granted: an unknown id, one that is not a string, another guest's, or one granted under a session a later pre-commit replaced. Nothing moves.
_prose.AUTHORIZATION_CLOSED: A tick or a release names a check that is already closed: reported, released, or closed by the stop. Nothing moves. A report that carries an event_id and is delivered twice is answered from its receipt and counts once.
_prose.SESSION_LIVE: A pre-commit arrived for a guest whose session is live and younger than the commitment period (VIP_COMMITMENT_HOURS, 24 by default). The session, its budget and its line are untouched. The answer names session_id and supersede_after, the time from which a pre-commit will be accepted. A larger budget, the same budget and a smaller one are refused alike: the commitment stands as it was made.
_prose.COMMITMENT_ACTIVE: From v0.2.16: a pre-commit arrived for a guest whose latest session stopped inside the commitment period, counted from when it was armed. Nothing is armed. The answer names session_id and precommit_after, the time from which a pre-commit is accepted. A larger, an equal and a smaller budget are refused alike.
_prose.TERMS_CHANGED: From v0.2.16: the pre-commit named a terms_version that is not the version in force, so the guest was shown other terms than the ones the engine would arm. Nothing is armed. The answer carries the terms_version in force.

event_vocabulary._rule: Every type this MVP writes to the append-only events table. The type is the first field hashed into the chain, so this list is part of the tamper-evidence surface, not documentation of it.
event_vocabulary._shared_with_package: precommit, policy.stop, redirect.issue, incentive.suppressed, eligibility.expired, stake.refused and stake.exceeded are the seven the package canon fixes, and they carry the same meaning in both. The remaining five (advisory.nudge, advisory.escalate, credit.redeem, rollover.apply and guest.erase) belong to this build alone and are not part of the specification.
event_vocabulary._schema_note: The events.type column is unconstrained TEXT; this canon is the only enumeration. A conforming implementation SHOULD constrain the column to this list.
event_vocabulary.precommit: a budget is armed; carries vip_id, session_id, budget and mode, the armed line, the eligibility and its determination time, and from v0.2.16 terms_version — the amount and the terms the guest agreed to, in one link of the chain
event_vocabulary.policy.stop: the session stops; carries the trigger (threshold, voluntary or suppression), consumed, preserved, redirect, rollover and residual, and the eligibility, capped and eligibility_expired flags; from v0.2.14 also overshoot_eur and authorizations_voided
event_vocabulary.redirect.issue: resort credits are issued from preserved budget; carries the split, the rollover and the residual
event_vocabulary.advisory.nudge: the advisory nudge line is crossed, announced once per session — including when one tick crosses both advisory lines, in which case the nudge is emitted before the escalation
event_vocabulary.advisory.escalate: the advisory escalation line is crossed, announced once per session
event_vocabulary.credit.redeem: an issued credit is redeemed — the point at which preserved budget becomes non-gaming revenue
event_vocabulary.rollover.apply: rollover credit is applied to a later session, extinguishing the liability
event_vocabulary.guest.erase: the display name erased on request; the audit trail and the chain survive intact
event_vocabulary.incentive.suppressed: incentive.suppressed is the engine declining to issue. scope=programme when a guest was removed from the programme, scope=settlement when a stop settled without an incentive, when a programme suppression lands on a stopped session whose settlement was not yet issued and now never will be, or at the issue call when the determination lapsed between the stop and that call — written once per session. It is written as its own link in the chain because a regulator asking this system to prove itself needs the occasions it did NOT reward, and an absent row proves nothing.
event_vocabulary.eligibility.expired: eligibility.expired records that a determination outlived its configured lifetime. It is written in addition to incentive.suppressed, never instead of it: the first says nobody refreshed the assessment, the second says nothing was issued.
event_vocabulary.stake.refused: the pre-stake check refused a stake in Hard-Stop; carries vip_id, session_id, the stake and the headroom it did not fit. It is written although the request that caused it fails
event_vocabulary.stake.exceeded: a tick reported, against a check, more consumption than the stake checked; carries vip_id, session_id, authorization_id, the stake and the amount consumed, which is counted in full

anchoring: Every policy decision is hash-chained: hash = sha256(prev_hash | type | timestamp | canonical payload), verifiable from genesis to head. Payloads carry opaque guest identifiers and euro amounts only, never a display name, so erasure never has to rewrite the chain.

privacy.rule: Erasing a synthetic display name preserves opaque IDs and the audit chain. The SQLite WAL must be checkpointed before completion. A blocking reader causes a retryable ERASURE_PENDING response. Backups and downstream copies have separate lifecycles.

paths.P1: Standalone — the MVP runs alone: guest screen, host console, admin. No integration required.
paths.P2: Downstream — dormant unless BOTH VIP_DOWNSTREAM_URL and VIP_DOWNSTREAM_KEY are set. Every dispatch names its source as vip-mvp/<version>, read from package.json, where the code reads its version. Event contract in INTEGRATION.md.
paths.note: P1/P2 are deployment paths of this MVP. They are not the operating modes: Hard-Stop and Advisory are the modes, and both run on either path.

model_figures._status: Synthetic by declaration. The seeded quarter is a reference model of one resort quarter, not a measurement of any operator. The console labels it as such on every screen.

_figure_kinds._rule: Labelling kept in a parallel map so every figure above stays the same JSON type it has always been. A label is never written over a value, because that destroys the machine-readability this file exists to provide.
_figure_kinds.limited_vips_per_quarter: ANCHORED — modelled count of VIPs who set a limit in the quarter. Mirrors the package canon.
_figure_kinds.preserved_per_vip_eur: ANCHORED — modelled preserved budget per limited VIP per quarter. Mirrors the package canon.
_figure_kinds.seed_budget_per_vip_eur: DERIVED — preserved_per_vip_eur ÷ (1 − thresholds.hard_stop_fraction) = 5100 ÷ 0.50. The smallest session budget consistent with the two figures above at the canon threshold; it is computed by the seed, not chosen.
_figure_kinds.redirected_quarter_eur: DERIVED — preserved_quarter_eur × the redirect split total (306,000 × 0.70)
_figure_kinds.non_gaming_capture: DERIVED — redirected_quarter_eur ÷ preserved_quarter_eur, which is the redirect split total by construction

model_figures._denominator_rule: The capture ratio is published against preserved budget — the slice of the pre-committed budget still unspent when the policy fires — and never against the guests' whole theoretical spend. The console prints that denominator beside the figure.
model_figures.boundary: Preserved budget is not new revenue. These figures price money the guest had already committed and would otherwise have taken out of the building; they are not a claim of incremental spend created.
model_figures._not_produced_here: Retention, churn, host hours and the cited odds ratio are comparison values. The admin console labels their origin. The engine only computes the local ledger.

config_authority.note: Environment variables named in .env.example and 04c_docker-compose.yml override at runtime within the canon ranges. Every value resolves to this file.

verification: npm test runs the baseline and regression suites. The full package also runs comparisons with the reference service and offline demos. See docs/FIXES.md in the repository root.
runtime: Node.js >= 22.13.0 (built-in node:sqlite). The module was added in 22.5.0 but required the --experimental-sqlite flag until 22.13.0 (and 23.4.0 on the 23 line), so 22.13.0 is the true floor for an unflagged `npm start`. Node 22's own documentation marks it Stability 1.1 — active development — and Node 22 prints an ExperimentalWarning on startup; that warning is expected and is not a fault of this build. The import is guarded: on an older runtime the process prints what is needed, what is running and the flag workaround, then exits 1. No compilation, no build step, no dependencies.
canon_change_log_2: 1.1 — the redirect split becomes a per-jurisdiction configurable in fact and not only in prose: three environment variables, validated by the same rule as every other threshold. The advisory nudge is now emitted when a single tick crosses both advisory lines at once; the previous build marked it as sent while emitting only the escalation, so a downstream reading the chain saw a session that escalated without ever being nudged. No threshold, split, model figure or event changed VALUE in this revision — what changed is where the split can be set from, and when an already-declared event fires.
_api_suppression_note: POST /v3/programme/suppress removes a guest from the incentive programme and stops any live session immediately under the suppressed settlement. Three reasons: exclusion, player_request, rg_determination. Accepts a vip_id the engine has never seen, so an exclusion register can pre-empt enrolment rather than racing it. Not reversible by this engine. A suppressed guest can neither redeem a credit nor apply a rollover in this build, whatever the reason: both answer INCENTIVE_SUPPRESSED.
canon_change_log_3: 1.2 — the eligibility gate, the reward cap and the suppression route, identical to the package canon at 1.3. Both ship at the reference setting, so no figure in this file changed value.
canon_change_log_4: 1.3 — the eligibility lifetime and the eligibility.expired event, identical to the package canon at 1.4. Ships unset, so no figure in this file changed value.
canon_change_log_5: 1.4 — cent-exact settlement closure, the non-negative delta guard, and migration at startup. No figure in this file changed value.
canon_change_log_6: 1.5 — GUEST_UNKNOWN and ALREADY_ERASED are raised through the engine's fail(code, status) helper, so they return the 404 and 409 this canon declares instead of the 500 that a bare Error produced through web.js's `err.status || 500`. The downstream envelope announces vip-mvp/0.2.5; it had said 0.2.3 on a v0.2.4 build, in this file's own code and in INTEGRATION.md. Every HTTP code in error_identifiers is an integer, with its sentence in _prose — a label never rewrites a value. The parity block now sends a NEGATIVE delta to both implementations and requires both to refuse it, which is the check whose absence let v3.10 ship the guard in this build and not in the reference. No threshold, split, model figure or event changed value.
canon_change_log_7: 1.6 — the parent pointer follows the package to v3.12. Nothing in this build changed behaviour; the package corrected its legal set. The field is rewritten in the same revision that bumps the package, which is what its own _version_rule requires.
canon_change_log_8: 1.7 — the parent pointer follows the package to v3.13. Two comments in this build that record when a fix landed — in src/boundary.js and test.js — had been rewritten by the bump to v0.2.6 to name v0.2.6; they name v0.2.5 again. canon_change_log_9: 1.8 — the parent pointer follows the package to v3.14. No change to this build's behaviour: the release notes in README.md state what each edition defines, which is what a note that ships to a buyer is for. No threshold, split, model figure, metric, event or route changed value.
canon_change_log_10: 1.9 — the parent pointer follows the package to v3.15. canon_change_log_11: 1.10 — the parent pointer follows the package to v3.16. No change to this build’s behaviour: the release note now names the third place where this build differs from the shipped reference — it writes the five events this canon scopes to it, beside the five the package canon fixes — and the note on the seeded quarter states the €5,100 preserved per VIP that the seed replays, so every figure this file carries is named in a document that ships with it.
canon_change_log_12: 1.11 — the parent pointer follows the package to v3.17, and this build takes the package's money rule: integer cents, fractions in integer millionths, each line the first cent at or above its fraction, and the settlement by largest remainder with ties to position — identical to slot 04b on every amount from €0.01 to €2,000.00. Attacked while running, the previous build answered four malformed inputs with a 500 or with the wrong answer where an identifier was owed — a vip_id that is not a string, a body that parses to anything but an object, a session_id that is not valid percent-encoding, and a credit_id of true, which redeemed credit 1 — and each now has its identifier and a check that fails without it. A vip_id armed as markup ran in the host console's browser; every string the pages print now passes through one escape function, and buttons carry their values in data attributes. An erased display name survived in the database file and its write-ahead log; it no longer does (privacy.rule). Every configuration the validation accepts now starts, seeds and serves — every redirect share at zero, the stop line at its lower bound and a jurisdiction-wide suppression each used to stop it at startup, and a determination lifetime is served with the seeded sessions settled under it — a refused configuration, a bad port included, is reported in one sentence with exit code 1 before any database exists, and the version in the pages, the banner and the downstream source is read from package.json; the source had still said 0.2.9. A suppressed guest can neither redeem a credit nor apply a rollover, whatever the reason; a pre-commit without a determination date is recorded without one, so a configured lifetime withholds its incentive; the Hard-Stop lock is stated as what it is — the session, with no gaming day; and the audit payloads and the NO_ROUTE body outside /v3 are named as the fourth divergence from slot 04b. A budget is taken to the nearest cent on arrival and consumption is read in whole cents from its exact total, so a tick carrying a fraction of a cent can no longer make consumed and preserved add up to a cent more than the budget, and ticks below a cent still add up; a suppression that lands on a stopped, unissued settlement, and a determination that lapses between the stop and the issue call, each write that refusal once as incentive.suppressed with scope settlement; and a port that is not a whole number is refused in one sentence. No threshold, split, model figure or event changed value.
canon_change_log_13: 1.12 — the parent pointer follows the package to v3.18, whose canon now opens with an intent block. No change to this build's behaviour.

release_behaviour.tick_replay: Optional event_id plus session_id deduplicates successful ticks. Enforced on both services.
release_behaviour.settlement: The published stop line is fixed for a session. A pending instrument cannot exceed either its original quote or the allocation allowed by the current policy. Withholding, expiry or tighter shares and caps return value to the guest.
release_behaviour.quarter: All credit totals use seeded stopped sessions. Rollover allocated at stop and still outstanding are separate balances.
release_behaviour.pre_stake_check: POST /v3/session/authorize reserves each stake against what is left to the published line and refuses one that does not fit; POST /v3/session/release returns a stake that was never played; a tick may name the check it reports. reserved_eur and headroom_eur are on the state. Enforced on both services.
release_behaviour.commitment_period: A live session younger than VIP_COMMITMENT_HOURS is not superseded: the pre-commit is refused with SESSION_LIVE. From v0.2.16 a session that stopped inside the same period refuses it with COMMITMENT_ACTIVE. Enforced on both services.
release_behaviour.terms: GET /v3/terms publishes the terms with their version; every pre-commit records the version beside the amount in the session, the state and the chain, and a pre-commit naming another version is refused with TERMS_CHANGED. Enforced on both services, with the same version for the same terms.
release_behaviour.defaults: From v0.2.16 VIP_REWARD_CAP_EUR defaults to 5000 and VIP_ELIGIBILITY_TTL_DAYS to 90; off switches either off. Unset or blank means the default on both services.

canon_change_log_14: 1.13 — MVP v0.2.13 ships with VIP SmartContract v3.19. Transactional writes, exact sub-cent accumulation, protected session quotes, tick receipts, eligibility checks and quarter reporting are covered by the regression suite.
canon_change_log_15: 1.14 — v0.2.14, with the package at v3.20. This build was made from the v0.2.13 that carries the transactional writes, exact sub-cent accumulation, tick receipts and protected quotes, which did not contain the pre-stake check published earlier under the same number. It is now in: POST /v3/session/authorize and POST /v3/session/release, a tick that may name the check it reports, reserved_eur and headroom_eur on the state, overshoot_eur and authorizations_voided on every stop, four identifiers and two events, identical to slot 04b. New in this revision: the commitment period. A pre-commit for a guest whose session is live and younger than VIP_COMMITMENT_HOURS (24) is refused with SESSION_LIVE; before, it replaced the session at once and moved the line. The store gains the authorizations table and two columns, added by the startup migration to a database an earlier build wrote. No threshold, split, model figure or existing event changed value.
canon_change_log_16: 1.15 — v0.2.15, with the package at v3.21: the open-source release. This build is released under the MIT License (LICENSE in this folder), terms says so, and the AS-IS notice and the licence note it used to carry are gone. No behaviour, threshold, split, model figure, route, status code, error identifier or event changed.
canon_change_log_17: 1.16 — v0.2.16, with the package at v3.22. Four changes of behaviour, on both services, after an outside review of v3.21. First, GET /v3/terms publishes the terms a guest agrees to with a version; every pre-commit records the version beside the amount, and one naming another version is refused with TERMS_CHANGED. Second, a stopped session holds the guest for the rest of the commitment period: a new pre-commit inside it is refused with COMMITMENT_ACTIVE. Third and fourth, the reward cap is on by default at €5,000 per stop and the determination lifetime at 90 days; off switches either off. No threshold, split or model figure changed value: the reference stop earns €4,590, under the default ceiling, and the seed records a fresh determination, so the seeded quarter is the canon quarter under the defaults too. The contract surface is nine /v3 routes; the error identifiers gain COMMITMENT_ACTIVE and TERMS_CHANGED; precommit carries terms_version.

reviewed_settlement.snapshot: New SQLite sessions retain the terms and exact on-line example. Confirmed client review, supplied terms version and configured-only are separately identified. Legacy agreements stay unknown.
reviewed_settlement.changed_rules: Pending benefits are limited by both the original agreement and active policy. Tighter restrictions return the difference to the guest. Stops and issuances record agreed and active versions and the reason.

canon_change_log_18: 1.17 — v0.2.17. Implements I-1, I-2 and I-3 through per-stop cap parity, reviewable allocations and an explicit withheld-benefit path. The reference model, thresholds, nine contract routes and author intent are preserved.
